title: The Forbidden Library No. 1: Dee's Obsidian Mirror
question: Would you gaze into this mirror?
facts: The mirror is held in the British Museum under registration number 1966,1001.1.
A 2021 study in Antiquity traced its obsidian to Pachuca, Mexico: an Aztec object, the kind of mirror tied to the god Tezcatlipoca ('Smoking Mirror').
John Dee recorded angelic sessions with the scryer Edward Kelley in the 1580s using 'shew-stones'; tradition, not Dee's own records, names this mirror as one of them.
Horace Walpole owned it at Strawberry Hill; his label reads: 'The Black Stone into which Dr Dee used to call his spirits.'
Kelley said the angels dictated the Enochian alphabet and calls to Dee during these sessions.

caption:
The British Museum holds Dr Dee's Aztec mirror.

Crafted from Mexican obsidian and linked to the god Tezcatlipoca, this dark artefact passed through the hands of Horace Walpole, bearing his note claiming Dee used it to summon spirits.

In the 1580s, Dee and his scryer Edward Kelley peered into such surfaces, recording an entire angelic lexicon.
